title: Mathematics — Grade 8 Entrance
subject: math

questions.prompt: Choose the part of a circle that is **not** a straight line.

Work out.

–6 × –13
Choose the letter that is the subject of the formula   πdh + 2πr² = A.

The diagram shows a pair of parallel lines with a straight line crossing them and some angles marked with letters.

Complete these sentences with the correct letters.

Angles ______ and ______ are alternate angles.

Angles ______ and ______ are corresponding angles.

Angles ______ and ______ are vertically opposite angles.
questions.criteria: Alternate angles: d and e. Corresponding angles: a and e (also accept c and d). Vertically opposite angles: c and e (also accept a and d). Award 2 marks for all three sentences correct; 1 mark for exactly two correct; otherwise 0.

Oliver writes this calculation.

questions.criteria: Award 1 mark for stating Oliver is not correct WITH a valid explanation based on the order of operations, e.g. the index and multiplication must be done before the addition: 5² = 25, 2 × 25 = 50, 1 + 50 = 51 (not 75). Simply saying 'not correct' with no valid reasoning scores 0.

Jamila has a 6-digit number.

Two of the digits in her number are hidden:

4 ■ ■ 3 5 6

For each of Jamila's statements, say whether it **must be true**, **could be true** or **must be false**.

1. My number is divisible by 4
2. My number is divisible by 5
3. My number is divisible by 8
4. My number is divisible by 9
questions.criteria: Correct answers: divisible by 4 — must be true (last two digits 56 are divisible by 4); divisible by 5 — must be false (the number ends in 6); divisible by 8 — must be false (last three digits 356 are not divisible by 8); divisible by 9 — could be true (digit sum is 18 + the two hidden digits, which may or may not be a multiple of 9). Award 2 marks for all four correct; 1 mark for two or three correct; otherwise 0.

questions.prompt:
Complete the table for   y = 2x − 1

| x | −2 |    | 2 |
|---|----|----|---|
| y |    | −3 |   |

Give the three missing values: y when x = −2, x when y = −3, and y when x = 2.
questions.answerKey: y = −5 (when x = −2); x = −1 (when y = −3); y = 3 (when x = 2)

questions.prompt:
Draw the graph of   y = 2x − 1   on the grid.

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot draw, describe the line in words, e.g. which points it passes through.]
questions.criteria: Award 1 mark for a correct straight line for y = 2x − 1 drawn (or clearly described) from x = −2 to x = 2, passing through the points (−2, −5), (−1, −3), (0, −1), (1, 1) and (2, 3).

questions.prompt:
Eva says, 'The highest common factor of 36 and 60 is 6'

Show that she is **not** correct.
questions.criteria: Award 1 mark for showing that 12 is a common factor of 36 and 60 that is greater than 6 (e.g. 36 = 12 × 3 and 60 = 12 × 5, so the HCF is 12, not 6). Any valid demonstration that the HCF is 12 earns the mark.

questions.answerKey: x = 120, y = 60 (accept any pair with x + y = 180 and x ≠ 90, x obtuse)

These are the lengths, in centimetres, for a sample of 10 freshwater fish.

6.9        7.6        7.8        6        5.7        6.5        5.1        7.2        7.1        7.8

Complete the stem-and-leaf diagram for this information, and give the key.

[Type your stem-and-leaf diagram, one stem per line, e.g. "5 | ...", and state the key.]
questions.criteria: Correct diagram: stems 5, 6, 7 with ordered leaves — 5 | 1 7;  6 | 0 5 9;  7 | 1 2 6 8 8. Award marks for: all 10 values included as correct leaves (1), leaves written in order within each stem (1), a correct key such as '5 | 1 means 5.1 cm' including the unit (1).

questions.prompt:
The lengths, in centimetres, of the sample of 10 freshwater fish were:

6.9        7.6        7.8        6        5.7        6.5        5.1        7.2        7.1        7.8

The table shows information about the lengths of 10 **saltwater** fish in a different sample.

|        | Saltwater |
|--------|-----------|
| Median | 8.4 cm    |
| Range  | 5.8 cm    |

Write **two** comparisons between the distribution of the lengths of the freshwater fish and the distribution of the lengths of the saltwater fish.

Give your comparisons in context.

You **must** include the statistics you use.
questions.criteria: Expected statistics for the freshwater fish: median = 7.0 cm and range = 7.8 − 5.1 = 2.7 cm. Award up to 2 marks per comparison: (1) a median comparison in context, e.g. the saltwater fish are on average longer because their median (8.4 cm) is greater than the freshwater median (7.0 cm); (2) a spread comparison in context, e.g. the saltwater fish lengths are more spread out / more varied because their range (5.8 cm) is greater than the freshwater range (2.7 cm). For each comparison: 1 mark for the correctly calculated freshwater statistic compared with the saltwater value, 1 mark for the correct interpretation in context (longer on average / more variable). Statistics must be stated to earn full marks.
